newsitem.title: USA: U.S. judge accepts Mitsubishi Paper plea.
newsitem.headline: U.S. judge accepts Mitsubishi Paper plea.

text.p: A U.S. District Court judge accepted late Tuesday a plea agreement in which Mitsubishi Paper Mills Ltd agreed to plead guilty to price-fixing charges and pay a $1.8 million fine.

Mitsubishi Paper, New Oji Paper Co Ltd and other Japanese fax paper manufacturers conspired to raise the price of fax paper sold in the United States by as much as 10 percent between July 1991 and early 1992, according to court papers. Charges were brought against the companies and each pleaded guilty, along with several of its executives named in the indictments.
First District Court Judge Mark Wolf declined to accept Mitsubishi's plea until he was assured an executive named in the indictment was no longer with the company.
